publication_scope.blurb: Ludwig Crocius — Book II Chapter 14 On the condition of those judged, namely eternal life. Densify COMPLETE (PHYS 430–mid-457): definition; constituents; porismata rejecting false goods; positive conclusions — Cap. 14 close. Cap. 15 starts mid PHYS 457 (De aeterna morte). Liber III starts PHYS 467.

source_text: CAPUT DECIMUMQUARTUM. De judicatorum conditione, & quidem nominatim de VITA AETERNA, quae finem hominis absolute summum ultimumque complectitur. Judicatorum conditio, in quam post hoc judicium deveniunt, aliis est vita & beatitudo aeterna, aliis mors, miseria & damnatio aeterna.
english: CHAPTER FOURTEEN. On the condition of those judged — and namely on ETERNAL LIFE, which embraces man's absolutely highest and last end.
The condition of those judged, into which they come after this judgment, for some is eternal life and beatitude, for others death, misery, and eternal damnation.

source_text: IV. Hucusque porismata: Sequuntur affirmationes. 1–2. Vera beatitudo in solo Deo. 3. Aeternae beatitudinis praemium in hac vita ab ea non separatur ut pignus. 4. Vita aeterna non in nobis & mundo, sed in Christo. 5. Imaginis divinae instauratio in homine incipit in hac vita. 6. Bonum vitae aeternae principale, unio videlicet cum Deo. 7. Diligens & religiosa vitae aeternae meditatio ad pietatem & peccati fastidium conducit — Cap. 14 close ante CAPUT DECIMUMQUINTUM de aeterna morte.
english: IV. So far the porismata: there follow affirmations. (1–2) True beatitude is in God alone. (3) The earnest of eternal beatitude in this life is not separated from it as a pledge. (4) Eternal life is not in us and the world, but in Christ. (5) Restoration of the divine image in man begins in this life. (6) The principal good of eternal life is union with God. (7) Diligent and religious meditation on eternal life leads to piety and loathing of sin — Cap. 14 close before CHAPTER FIFTEEN on eternal death.

source_text: 8. Neque est favor regum, principum, aliorum — affentatione plus quam merito. 10. Neque est in uxore & liberis — sunt extra nos; amittuntur; vertuntur saepe in malum; non aeternant. 11. Sicut summum bonum neque corporis neque externis bonis continetur, ita neque animi bonis solis. 12. Neque in his bonis corporis & animi simul sumtis.
english: (8) Nor is it the favor of kings, princes, and others — more by flattery than by desert.
(10) Nor is it in wife and children — they are outside us; they are lost; they often turn to evil; they do not eternalize.
(11) Just as the highest good is contained neither in goods of the body nor in external goods, so neither in goods of the mind alone. (12) Nor in these goods of body and mind taken together.

source_text: 3. Neque est opulentia — immoderatum cumulandarum opum studium; opum acquisitio plena laboris; qui amplas opes tot periculis exponit. 6. Neque est in magnificis & superbis aedificiis. 7. Neque in nobilitate — plena laboris; quod boni in nobilitate est fragile; non perenne & stabile.
english: (3) Nor is it wealth — the immoderate zeal of heaping up riches; acquiring wealth is full of toil; he who has ample riches exposes them to so many dangers.
(6) Nor is it in magnificent and proud buildings. (7) Nor in nobility — full of toil; whatever good is in nobility is fragile; it is not a perennial and stable good.

source_text: II. Hinc inferuntur sequentia porismata. 1. Summa hominis beatitudo non est voluptas carnis. 2. Neque est in rebus secundis divinae providentiae subjectis — quia mortales caecos reddit; prudentissime cogitata pessimis successibus implicat; ingenti tristitia afficit; facit ut insololescant; variam in mutabilitate constantiam servat.
english: II. From this the following porismata are inferred. (1) Man's highest beatitude is not the pleasure of the flesh.

(2) Nor is it in secondary things subject to divine providence — because it blinds mortals; entangles the most prudently planned with the worst outcomes; afflicts with great sadness; makes men insolent; and keeps a strange constancy in its very mutability.

source_text: II. Vita aeterna est civium regni Dei absoluta immunitas a peccato, Satana & impiorum tyrannide, omnique miseria, & cum hac conjuncta aeterna & plenissima omnis boni fruitio in beata Dei visione & communione, perfecta animae & corporis glorificatione, divinae imaginis instauratione, consortio sanctorum angelorum omniumque piorum jucundissimo, laetitia inexhausta ad Dei gloriam perfecte celebrandam. Vitam dicimus electorum beatitudinem protecto & juventium statu, per metonymiam subjecti — hic vivere est beatum esse. Aeternam dicimus ad differentiam tum vitae corporalis temporalis, tum spiritualis fidelium in hoc mundo, quae est gradus & principium aeternae illius vitae nunc absconditae cum Christo in Deo, Col. 3.v.3.
english: II. Eternal life is the citizens of God's kingdom's absolute immunity from sin, Satan and the tyranny of the impious, and every misery, and joined with this the eternal and fullest fruition of every good in the blessed vision and communion of God, perfect glorification of soul and body, restoration of the divine image, most joyful fellowship of holy angels and all the pious, and unexhausted joy for perfectly celebrating God's glory.

We call it life by metonymy of the subject for the elect's beatitude in a protected and youthful state — here to live is to be blessed. We call it eternal to differ both from temporal bodily life and from the faithful's spiritual life in this world, which is a degree and beginning of that eternal life now hidden with Christ in God (Col. 3:3).

source_text: 3. Est civium regni Dei, Heb. 11 &c. 4. Consistit tum in malorum contrariorum remotione, tum in bonorum positivi accessu — visione Dei, glorificatione, consortio sanctorum, laetitia. Visio Dei est essentiale beatitudinis. Essentia Dei infinita; haec visio si stative consideretur; naturalia in Deo; personarum ratio; decretorum alia ratio. Consortium sanctorum angelorum. Vitae aeternae finis — Dei gloria. Summa igitur hominis beatitudo est in soli Deo.
english: (3) It belongs to the citizens of God's kingdom (Heb. 11, &c.). (4) It consists both in the removal of contrary evils and in the access of positive goods — the vision of God, glorification, fellowship of the saints, joy. The vision of God is essential to beatitude. God's essence is infinite; this vision if considered statically; what is natural in God; the reason of the persons; another reason of the decrees. Fellowship of the holy angels. The end of eternal life is God's glory. Therefore man's highest beatitude is in God alone.
